title: Horizon and Passage
premise: Ada Montrose, a salvage diver scraping a living off a wreck the navy pretends doesn't exist, is hired by her old rival Cassian Vey for a job her late father swore the crew would never take: raising the Passage, a lost survey vessel carrying sealed cargo that cost Ada's mother her life. Racing a rival salvage fleet and a six-tide deadline, Ada descends into the drowned ship and discovers the cargo is a ledger proving the navy deliberately sank the Passage — and that her mother died trying to surface it. Betrayed by Vey, hunted by both fleets, Ada must choose between selling the truth for her crew's survival or giving it away to honor the woman she barely remembers. In the end she surfaces the ledger herself, loses the salvage money but keeps her crew and gains Vey's grudging loyalty, and lets the sea keep its dead while the living carry the truth ashore.
about_author: Sable Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wreck reports along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who make their living from other people's disasters.

chapters.title: Cold Water Work
chapters.summary: Ada Montrose dives the unnamed navy wreck at dawn, salvaging brass while her crew watches the horizon for patrol boats. POV: Ada. Establishes her competence, the crew's poverty, and her rule against certain wrecks. Emotional beat: weary pride in work that keeps them fed but going nowhere.

chapters.title: The Man Who Left
chapters.summary: Cassian Vey walks into the harbor tavern offering triple rates for a job he won't fully describe. Ada throws him out; her quartermaster Bram quietly takes his card. POV: Ada. Flashback fragments reveal their shared history and the job they swore off after her father's death. Emotional beat: old anger reopening an old wound.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: The crew votes: the boat needs a new engine or they're done by winter. They accept Vey's contract — the Passage, sunk twenty years ago in restricted water. POV: Bram, showing the vote through the eyes of a man who loved Ada's father. Emotional beat: hope tangled with dread.

chapters.title: What Her Father Swore
chapters.summary: Ada rereads her father's logbook and finds the oath page torn out. She confronts Vey, who admits the Passage carried something the families of the lost were never told. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve; she joins the dive not for money but for answers.

chapters.title: Departure on the Ebb
chapters.summary: The crew sails north through fog, evading a coast guard cutter that seems to know their route. First hints someone inside the fleet is leaking information. POV: Juno, the young diver who idolizes Ada. Emotional beat: nervous excitement, the sea feeling watchful.

chapters.title: The Graveyard Shelf
chapters.summary: They reach the site above a trench where three wrecks lie broken. Sonar shows another vessel shadowing them beyond the shelf. POV: Ada. First dive on the Passage reveals it was holed from the inside — scuttled, not sunk. Emotional beat: cold shock beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Names on the Manifest
chapters.summary: In the flooded chart room Ada finds a manifest listing her mother as passenger, not crew — a fact every record denies. POV: Ada, intercut with memory fragments of her mother. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity; the woman she mourned was never who she was told.

chapters.title: Vey's Confession
chapters.summary: Vey admits he was a junior officer aboard the navy ship that fired on the Passage; the job is his penance. Ada refuses to forgive him. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: guilt offered like a wound, refused like charity.

chapters.title: The Other Boat
chapters.summary: The rival salvage fleet — Harrow & Sons, navy contractors — arrives and issues a warning shot across their bow. Three tides left. POV: Juno, terrified during the standoff. Emotional beat: fear sharpening the crew into something harder than a family.

chapters.title: Descent Past Safe Depth
chapters.summary: Ada dives below safe limits to reach the sealed strongroom, guided by Vey's knowledge of naval construction. She nearly dies when her line fouls; Bram hauls her back. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the wilderness forgives nothing — and she went anyway.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada recovers a waterproof case containing the Passage's true cargo: a ledger documenting illegal arms shipments the navy sank to bury. Her mother was the courier who tried to save it. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: triumph and horror arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Bram's Bargain
chapters.summary: Harrow's men board under cover of dark and offer Bram double to hand over the case. He refuses, but Juno sees the meeting and misreads it. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and proven, then poisoned by suspicion.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: A storm closes in; the crew demands they run for port with the ledger. Ada insists on one more dive to recover her mother's personal effects. The crew splits. POV: Juno, caught between mentors. Emotional beat: love against duty, wearing ordinary faces.

chapters.title: Two Tides
chapters.summary: With two tides left, Harrow's flagship moves to physically block the site. Vey proposes a decoy run through the reef channel only he knows. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: redemption gambled with other people's lives.

chapters.title: The Reef Run
chapters.summary: Night passage through the reef; the decoy works until a rogue swell cripples the boat's steering. They limp into a hidden cove as the storm breaks. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: exhausted relief that costs them their engine and their head start.

chapters.title: What the Sea Kept
chapters.summary: Final dive: Ada retrieves her mother's effects and finds a letter addressed to 'my daughter, if she ever comes looking.' She reads it in the cove by lamplight. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the meeting death postponed for twenty years.

chapters.title: Harrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Cornered in the cove, Ada meets Elias Harrow, who offers to buy the ledger and protect the crew — the same deal, he implies, her father took and died regretting. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy; she understands her father at last.

chapters.title: The Choice at Slack Water
chapters.summary: Last tide before Harrow's deadline. Ada chooses neither sale nor silence: she photographs every page and mails copies to three newspapers, keeping the original as proof. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into certainty.

chapters.title: Running the Blockade
chapters.summary: The crippled boat makes a desperate daylight run past Harrow's flagship; Vey takes the wheel through gunfire and is wounded shielding Juno. Coast guard intercepts — called, it turns out, by Bram's earlier anonymous tip. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: sacrifice rewriting old debts.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Detained aboard the cutter, Ada hands the ledger to a sympathetic investigator as Harrow's lawyers descend. The story breaks on the wire before the navy can contain it. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the moment private grief becomes public truth.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: Weeks later: hearings announced, Harrow arrested, Vey recovering and uninvited-but-present at the harbor. Ada scatters her mother's effects' ashes at the wreck site's coordinates. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: mourning completed; identity reclaimed on her own terms.

chapters.title: Passage
chapters.summary: Spring: the crew refits with settlement money, refusing Vey's offer of a funded expedition and instead hiring him as an equal partner. They sail for open water with no contract but their own. POV: Ada, closing the logbook her father began. Emotional beat: survival paid for, love chosen freely, the horizon finally theirs.
